observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a squat, wide, low reptile seen from the front, head lowered toward the camera, splayed clawed forelimbs, with a mound of overlapping rust-red plates rising behind the head. East: a long, low-slung lizard-like body in profile, belly almost on the ground, head pointing right, short splayed legs. A row of long rust-red blade-like plates lies flat along the spine, overlapping like folded fins. The tail ends in a smaller cluster of fanned red fin-blades. North: the same animal from behind, haunches and hind legs splayed, the stacked red dorsal plates as a rounded dome, and a short vertical column of red plates down the middle (the tail seen end-on). All three are the same height; north is visibly narrower than south.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution: a broad, heavy head facing the camera with small dark eyes and a down-turned mouth, a thick neck, clawed forefeet splayed outward, and layered red plates that form a hump over the back. The silhouette is wide and low and reads a little like a tortoise or horned lizard seen head-on. Painterly shading, clean edges, no backdrop.
observed.east.png: Side profile: a slender, elongated, sprawling-gait body with a pointed snout and tucked legs, its pose low and coiled as if waiting in ambush. About eight long overlapping rust-coloured fin-blades run flat from the nape to the hips and continue into a fanned tuft of smaller blades at the tail tip. Brown skin with a pale belly stripe. The rendering is painterly and realistic, with no shadow under the body.
observed.north.png: Rear view: wide hips, splayed hind legs and clawed feet, and the dorsal blades stacked into a dome over the back. The tail tip's blades form a narrow vertical column at the midline. There is no face and no eyes. The silhouette is narrower than the south view, with less body mass showing beside the plates.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about 2 cells long and roughly ankle-to-knee high beside the vanilla human: a low, ground-hugging animal. At normal play (32 px/cell) it reads as a small brown elongated shape with a reddish back, similar in length to the rat thumbnail but longer.

edits.change: The south view shows a slender, wedge-shaped head with narrow jaws and forward-set eyes toward the viewer. The fin-blade row rises behind the head as a separate ridged crest on the neck and shoulders, with the head clearly distinct from it and no rounded shell-like dome.

Build an alien anatomy from the description alone: a long, flat, low-slung torso. Four short limbs fold in close beneath the body, ending in narrow pads rather than splayed claws. A long, tapering neck-and-head wedge leads the body. The silhouette is a flat wedge, not a monitor lizard or tortoise.

The north view is the rear view, seen from behind. The hips and flanks are as wide as the south view's shoulders. The haunches are full and heavy, and the dorsal blade row spans the same width as on south.
The north view carries the same substantial torso and haunch volume as the east and south views, with the thighs bulging out to both sides of the spine.

The tail ends in one broad fan of blades. The east view shows the fan spread wide to both sides of the tail. The north view shows the same fan seen from behind, spreading evenly left and right around the tail root, as wide as the haunches.

invariants: Low ambusher posture, body held close to the ground
Row of dorsal fins along the spine, folded flat when running
Smaller fan of fins on the tail
Fully transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, clean dark outline

Same palette and body proportions across all facings
request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the dakkra. A low ambusher that waits in shade, then makes a short, fast rush at exposed prey. It spreads a row of dorsal fins and a smaller tail fan to shed heat in shade, and folds both flat when it runs. Body plan, identical in every view: a long, flat, low-slung wedge-shaped torso held close to the ground, with four short limbs tucked close beneath it, ending in narrow pads. The head is a slender wedge with narrow jaws and forward-set eyes. It sits at the end of a tapering neck. The torso is substantial, with full, heavy haunches, and the hips are as wide as the shoulders. The dorsal fin blades form a separate ridged crest rising along the spine behind the head, from the shoulders to the tail root. Its width is the same in every view. The tail ends in one broad fan of blades spreading evenly to both sides. Front view: eyes toward the viewer, the slender wedge head in front, the ridged crest rising behind it. Side view: the long flat torso, the crest along the spine, the broad tail fan at the rear. Rear view, seen from behind: the full-width haunches and flanks, the crest spanning the same width as in the front view, and the broad tail fan spreading left and right from the tail root, with the eyes hidden. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, soft painted edges in a deeper shade of the local colour, clean dark outline. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background: no ground, no water, no shadow, no text, no border.
